profile.reading:
Csquare IAD4-A sits at 21561 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, Virginia 20147, one of two street addresses, 21561 and 21571 Beaumeade Circle, that Csquare's own spec sheet lists under its single "IAD4" campus heading. Csquare, formerly branded Centersquare, was launched in April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, with Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business held by Brookfield since 2019. Csquare went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists only one Virginia "IAD4_A" line item, 58,939 square feet sellable and 77.8 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, treating IAD4 as a single reportable leased asset despite the two street addresses on the public spec sheet. This profile assigns that SEC figure to this specific address, since the SEC line-item name "IAD4_A" matches this building's "-A" suffix, while flagging that Csquare's SEC disclosure does not itself separately break out IAD4-A from IAD4-B. Csquare's public spec sheet states a campus-wide 57,927 square feet of raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity, with standard cage density up to 300 watts per square foot, and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for this campus. Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, as a matter of public record.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley hosts dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of Csquare's IAD4 campus. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and separately discloses that the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked across this dataset. IAD4 is a two-building campus, IAD4-A and IAD4-B, on adjoining Beaumeade Circle addresses, distinct from Csquare's Sterling IAD1 and IAD2 campuses several miles away, and the campus-wide power and floor-space totals published by Csquare cover both buildings together, so this address alone should not be read as independently drawing the full campus figure. Prospective tenants should confirm current pricing and available capacity directly with Csquare rather than relying on the March 2026 SEC snapshot, which predates this record's research date by several months.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement (IAD4 reported as single asset "IAD4_A")

profile.research_note: Sqft is the SEC S-1 line item named "IAD4_A" (58,939 sqft sellable, 77.8% leased), attributed to this row since its own SEC line-item name matches this building's "-A" suffix, though Csquare's public spec sheet groups both IAD4-A and IAD4-B addresses under one undifferentiated campus heading. Power figures (35.8MW utility, 16.8MW UPS, 20MW generator) are campus-wide only, so no capacity figure was attributed. Cage density "up to 300 watts/sqft" is a ceiling, not a typical figure. reading.body:
IAD4-A is a 58,939 square foot colocation facility at one of two Ashburn addresses under Csquare's IAD4 campus heading. The campus publishes 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity across both addresses combined, with a cage density ceiling of 300 watts per square foot. The facility holds SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads including payment systems and federal compliance requirements.

At the campus-wide 35.8 megawatts of utility power and a typical AI training density assumption of 40 kilowatts per rack, the full IAD4 facility could serve roughly 900 racks of accelerator hardware. Csquare's SEC filing shows 77.8 percent of the 58,939 square feet attributed to this building was leased as of March 31, 2026, indicating active customer occupancy. The operator does not publish which tenants occupy the space, the specific power allocation between IAD4-A and IAD4-B, or the year the facility opened.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities and publishes power capacity for 23 of them, totaling 1,375.4 megawatts. IAD4 ranks twenty-fourth among published Virginia capacity, representing 2.6 percent of the state's disclosed power. Ashburn's Data Center Alley concentrates the world's largest colocation market within a few miles, with Csquare operating four Northern Virginia campuses among dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators served by Dominion Energy.
